messages:
aj: Heads up — noticed a short but sharp spike in per-token p75 and p95 on pool-dedicated-eu-west-1 around 08:42 UTC. It lines up with a bunch of kernel switch logs in the runtime profiler. KV cache hit-rate dipped ~12% at the same time. 

carla: Seen it. Dashboard: https://console/redwood/dashboards/pool-dedicated-eu-west-1/token-latency — the stacked token breakdown shows a jump in 'kernel_switch_wait' and 'kv_fetch_ms'.

marco: I pulled a flamegraph and a perf trace: looks like when kernel selector switched from fast-f32 -> int8-path it caused extra memcpy + kernel init on a subset of requests. attaching prom queries I used: 

marco: ```
# token latency by stage (PromQL)
sum(rate(runtime_token_latency_bucket{pool="dedicated-eu-west-1"}[1m])) by (le,stage)

# KV cache hit rate per-pool
(sum(rate(kvcache_hits_total{pool="dedicated-eu-west-1"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kvcache_requests_total{pool="dedicated-eu-west-1"}[5m]))) * 100
```

ops-bot: alert: pool-dedicated-eu-west-1 token-p95 exceeded 450ms for 30s at 2026-03-14T08:42:12Z (severity: medium)

laura: Did we change batching heuristics or routing policy in the canary earlier today? If a route moved to a different oxford kernel variant that could trigger kernel init.

aj: Not that I'm aware of at app-layer. We had an autoscaler event that drained 2 nodes (scale-in) + the canary for quantized-int8 landed on the same pool within the same minute. Might be coincidental but suspicious.

carla: KV behaviour looks odd: kvcache_evictions spiked. Possible noisy-neighbor seq-len patterns flushed hot prefixes. I added a short query to correlate per-route prefix hit rates: 

carla: ```
# per-route prefix hit rate
sum by(route)(rate(kvcache_prefix_hits_total{pool="dedicated-eu-west-1"}[5m])) / sum by(route)(rate(kvcache_prefix_requests_total{pool="dedicated-eu-west-1"}[5m]))
```

marco: From the profiler, affected requests had long prompt prefixes + the routing split caused smaller batches which disabled continuous batching fast-path. So two orthogonal things: kernel warmup + batching fragmentation.

laura: For dashboards, suggest adding a per-pool "headroom index": free_batch_slots / max_batch_slots and a kernel-churn counter (kernel_switches_total by pool). That will make noisy neighbor or churn visible.

aj: Agreed. Proposal: add two small panels: 1) headroom index 2) kernel churn heatmap (time vs node). Also add an annotation for autoscaler events so we can see scale-in/out overlays.

devex-bot: FYI: rollout-tracker: canary quant-int8 deployed to pool-dedicated-eu-west-1 at 08:41:45 UTC (id: roll-20260314-17)

marco: Quick mitigation: we can temporarily pin the canary variant to dedicated-canary pool (isolated) and force warmup probe for kernels on first allocation: run small warmup batch on model load to avoid per-request init. I can prepare a patch.

carla: Also recommend adding a per-route token-latency waterfall visualization (parse tokens into stages: queue, batch_wait, kernel_init, compute, kv_fetch, encode). That helped us debug the last noisy-neighbor incident.

aj: Action items:
- marco: patch to add warmup probe + kernel init metric (T+1)
- carla: add headroom + kernel_churn panels + autoscaler annotations (T+2)
- laura: schedule a short canary isolation for quant-int8 and re-run synthetic traffic for 20m (T+3)

laura: I'll take ownership of tracking this in the dedicated capacity dashboard and will mark it as an incident if we see repeat occurrences. :white_check_mark:

aj: Thanks — I'll follow up with traces and the flamegraph links in the incident thread. If anyone sees p95 spikes on other pools please @aj.

marco: patch draft up next, pinging runtime-owners for review.

carla: leaving a quick note — we should also store the per-route prefix hit-rate as a rolling percentile to avoid noisy instantaneous dips.

aj: great point. ok closing for now, will open follow-ups in #incidents if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:
